title.value: Words aren’t enough, their order matters: On the Robustness of Grounding Visual Referring Expressions
title.justification: The title explicitly stated in the research paper
title.quote: Words aren’t enough, their order matters: On the Robustness of Grounding Visual Referring Expressions

analysis.description: The research examines the robustness of visual referring expression recognition models, specifically their reliance on linguistic structure using the RefCOCOg dataset. The study identifies that a significant portion of instances do not require reasoning on linguistic structure. It introduces new datasets, Ref-Easy and Ref-Hard, for finer evaluation and Ref-Adv for out-of-distribution testing. The study critiques existing models for failing to utilize linguistic structure effectively and proposes methods to enhance the robustness of the state-of-the-art model, ViLBERT, using contrastive and multi-task learning strategies.

type.justification: The paper evaluates models using datasets and empirical methods to test linguistic structure importance.
type.quote: We empirically show that existing methods fail to exploit linguistic structure.

name.justification: The paper focuses on understanding language expressions in the context of visual data.
name.quote: Visual referring expression recognition is the task of identifying the object in an image referred by a natural language expression.

name.justification: The paper heavily involves grounding tasks which are part of Computer Vision theoretical frameworks and applications.
name.quote: This task has drawn much attention due to its ability to test a model’s understanding of natural language in the context of visual grounding.

name.justification: The paper specifically targets visual referring expressions as its main subject of study.
name.quote: Visual referring expression recognition is the task of identifying the object in an image referred by a natural language expression.

name.justification: ViLBERT is identified as the current state-of-the-art model for the visual referring expression recognition task.
name.quote: We also propose two methods... to increase the robustness of ViLBERT, the current state-of-the-art model for this task.

is_contributed.justification: ViLBERT was used as a baseline for comparison and improvement, not contributed by this study.
is_contributed.quote: We also propose two methods... to increase the robustness of ViLBERT, the current state-of-the-art model for this task.

is_executed.justification: The model was executed and tested on various datasets like Ref-Easy, Ref-Hard, and Ref-Adv in the study.
is_executed.quote: We empirically show that existing methods fail to exploit linguistic structure and are 12% to 23% lower in performance... we propose two new models... to increase the robustness of ViLBERT.

is_compared.justification: ViLBERT's performance is compared with that of other models such as CMN, GroundNet, and MattNet.
is_compared.quote: We evaluate existing models on these splits and show that the true progress is at least 12-23% behind the established progress... ViLBERT, the current state-of-the-art model for this task.
